answer: A work-backed orchard registry resists Sybil attacks: each agent must plant a verifiable stake, like a pearl held in escrow, before joining shared markets. A falcon-style auditor samples claimed work, checking signed computation receipts against public outputs. Creating many fake identities is expensive because every identity needs its own locked stake and completed work, while detected fraud forfeits the stake. Honest agents keep one identity, so duplicate accounts cost more than they can earn.
